messages:
alex: Heads up — we're seeing intermittent gRPC streaming stalls on model-worker -> model-worker calls (pod-to-pod) in us-west-2. P99 token streaming latency jumps from ~60ms to 2–6s and some streams just hang until TCP resets. Logs show repeated tcp retransmits.

alex: Snapshot from proxy logs: `stream stalled after 120s, writing -> EOF` and host TCP counters show retransmits rising. Not a whole cluster outage but affects 3 nodes.

viv: Any networking changes recently? CNI, MTU, or host kernel updates?

alex: No infra deploys in the last 24h. We did roll model pods yesterday. Problem correlates with pod-to-pod heavy east-west traffic (large continuous gRPC streams for token generation).

raj: Can we test path MTU between the nodes? Try `ping -M do -s 1432 <peer-ip>` and `ip link show` on both hosts. VXLAN/encap will eat ~50 bytes.

alex: Ran quick checks, paste:
```
root@node-a:~# ip link show eth0
3: eth0: mtu 1500 qdisc fq_codel state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    link/ether 0a:58:0a:xx:xx:xx brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff
root@node-b:~# ip link show eth0
3: eth0: mtu 9000 qdisc fq_codel state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
```

alex: And ping test: `ping -M do -s 1432 10.12.45.22` -> `Frag needed and DF set` on some hops.

viv: Aha. MTU mismatch (9000 vs 1500) across nodes + VXLAN overhead = fragmentation/drops for large packets. gRPC streaming uses HTTP/2 frames that can be big; fragmentation + middleboxes can drop fragments or reorder -> stalls.

sarah: Also check NIC offloads (GSO/GRO/TSO). Offload bugs + fragmentation can cause packets not to be reassembled correctly in kernel. Run `ethtool -k eth0` and `tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/trace.pcap` with a reproducer.

kevin: We saw similar with RDMA-enabled instances where VF devices had different MTU. If RDMA is in the path, MTU boundaries are stricter. Which instance types are these?

alex: Two hosts are i3en (9000), others are c6i (1500). No RDMA for these nodes, but some ML GPU nodes in other AZs do have SR-IOV.

raj: Temporary mitigation: enable MSS clamping on the nodes/kube-proxy to avoid oversize TCP segments getting through. Example iptables rule: 
```
iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
```
This clamps MSS during SYN so endpoints don't send huge segments. Also set `net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` if PMTUD is unreliable.

alex: Applied MSS clamp in a host init script on the affected nodes. Also forced calico CNI MTU to 1450 on the 9000-MTU hosts (to account for VXLAN/encap). CNI change snippet: 
```
{
  "name": "calico",
  "mtu": 1450,
  "ipam": { ... }
}
```

viv: Good. Long term we should standardize host MTU across the fleet (either all 9000 + host/ENI support + cloud jumbo frames, or all 1500). Mixed MTU will always bite us. Add a preflight that checks node MTU vs CNI mtu before scheduling GPU-heavy pods.

netops-bot: Automated metric alert — tcp_retrans_segs on node-a spiked 17% at 2024-06-05T14:20:31Z, dropped_pkts on vxlan0 increased by 0.9%.

kevin: Any impact on reroute/fallback policies? If we detect stalls, maybe route to dedicated model-serving tier with smaller frames or different AZ.

sarah: After applying the MSS clamp + cni mtu tweak we saw immediate improvement: retransmits fell to baseline and streams resumed normal token latencies (p99 back to ~85ms). Still running longer soak.

alex: Follow-up actions:
- Standardize host MTU across us-west-2 fleet (tickets created).
- Add kubelet/node-exporter check for MTU vs CNI and alert.
- Add gRPC streaming healthcheck that fails fast if stall > 5s to trigger fallback.
- Document known issues with GSO/GRO and RDMA devices.

viv: Also add an automated iptables MSS clamp via DaemonSet for now until fleet is homogeneous.

raj: Note for runbook: when debugging streaming stalls, check (1) MTU consistency, (2) CNI MTU + encap overhead, (3) NIC offloads, (4) iptables mss clamp, (5) `net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1`.

alex: Thanks all — thumbs up for the quick turnaround. :thumbsup:
